name: Hengifoss and Litlanesfoss
why: Up a gorge to Litlanesfoss in its basalt columns, then to Hengifoss, a 128 m fall on a cliff striped with red clay.
book: Free; paid parking by Lagarfljót, 35 km south of Egilsstaðir on road 931. Café and toilets at the car park.
water: Tap at the car park; carry 0.5 litre.
dangers: The first part is steep; muddy after rain.
Do not walk to the foot of Hengifoss: falling rocks.

points.name: Hengifoss car park by Lagarfljót
points.note: By the long lake Lagarfljót; steps lead up the slope from the café.

points.name: Litlanesfoss
points.note: After 30 minutes: a 30 m fall framed by tall basalt columns.

points.name: Hengifoss viewpoint
points.note: Hengifoss falls 128 m down a black basalt cliff with thin red clay layers between the lava flows.
